build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not module 1: its packed bytes end at $CE24 (1,061 bytes, the same on sides 1, 2 and 4); the unpacker reads on to the end of its four-sector window, so these are module 3's packed bytes (side 1) decoded with module 1's table. Nothing reads them

comments.text: Location module 1, the shop. The game runs it for a square whose action record (at $5F/$60) starts with $81 (game $8845: JSR $03BF with A = 1, then JSR $CA00). Loads the item table that record byte 6 names (load_item_table $03BC: file $75 of T35/L15 to $3100), keeps the picture state $AB/$AC on the stack, copies the shop's name, record bytes 7-18, to the location name at $F4D0 and shows picture 1 from the buffer at $E000 ($041C). Then $9D/$9E = record + $13, the $FF-ended list of item classes the shop deals in; $74 = byte 3 (buy_price's shift), $73 = byte 4 (sell_price's shift), byte 5 (the greeting) into shop_greeting_op; party_changed = 0. The loop at $CA4E: roster shown, the greeting printed from the map's text (print_map_message), 'Who wants to enter?' (pick_member; skipped in a party of one, which uses member 1); a member who is not conscious gets 'can't buy anything' and the loop starts again; otherwise 'Do you want to B)uy or S)ell?' runs shop_buy or shop_sell and the loop starts again. Left-arrow at that question (shop_cancel $CA98) goes back to the member question, or, in a party of one, straight to shop_exit ($CA8D) without the save_game test. Left-arrow at the member question leaves: save_game ($02D8) when party_changed is set, $AB/$AC put back, the map stream the picture overwrote unpacked again ($03C5), carry set, so the game clears the message area and redraws ($8872 -> $AC8C).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CA59, written at $CA4B from byte 5 of the shop's map record: the number of the map message that greets the party each time round the loop (print_map_message $0317, from the current map's text block).

S)ell, for the trading member at ($66). count_items_of_classes ($037A, the class list at $9D) counts the items the shop will take; none: message 5, 'You don't have anything they want!'. Otherwise message 7 (window cleared, the '$$$ ITEM' header) and the list at $CADC: its items are the member's slots 1-30 ($4D = 31, $4E = count + 1), sell_list_line prints each through $47/$48, 'P' is the extra key ($BE = $D0), then the P)ool line and list_choose. A slot chosen: unequip_slot ($0362), its item and count bytes zeroed, sell_price added to the cash (cash_add $0356, which saturates), the line flashed ($03A1), the item's stock (byte 2 of its record) raised by one unless it is already 255, item_table_changed and party_changed set, and the list shown again; when the sale leaves nothing the shop takes ($CB41-$CB49), the routine leaves at once through $CB51, which writes the table back. 'P' pools the party's cash on the member ($038F); left-arrow returns, through save_item_table ($03C2) when the table changed ($CB51).

Per-item routine of the sell list: list_show_page calls it through $47/$48 with A = a slot number, 1-30. Declines (carry set, $CBAC) an empty slot or an item whose class the shop does not take (item_class_in_list $03D1, list at $9D). Otherwise starts the line (list_line_label $03A7), prints sell_price right-aligned in five columns ($02ED), a space and the item's name in the singular (set_count_one $04DE, print_item_name $03CB), in inverse video when the slot is the equipped armour (+$25) or weapon (+$1F); carry clear.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CB92, written at $CB63: the slot sell_list_line is printing, compared with the character's armour slot (+$25) and weapon slot (+$1F) to show an equipped item in inverse video.

B)uy, for the trading member at ($66). No free slot (find_free_slot $0341): message 8, 'Your inventory is full.'. Otherwise message 7 (window cleared, '$$$ ITEM') and the list at $CBCC: count_stock counts items 1-93 in stock that the shop sells (none: message 1, 'We are temporarily out of stock.', and return); $4E = that count, $4D = 94, buy_list_line prints each line through $47/$48, 'P' is the extra key. An item chosen (A and $49): record_address ($039E) points $16/$17 at its record, buy_price, and cash_compare ($03D4) sends a price above the cash to $CC4A ('That costs too much!', play_sound_1 ($0232), whose sound record 11 never sets the gate bit, so nothing is heard, and a pause). Otherwise the item goes into the first free slot with record byte 4 (a gun's clip size, the charges of a stack) as its count byte, spend_cash ($03CE) pays, the line flashes, the stock (record byte 2) drops by one (255 included), both change flags are set and the list is shown again; when the slots run out, play_sound_1 (silent) and 'Your inventory is full.'. 'P' pools the party's cash on the member; left-arrow returns. Left-arrow and a full inventory leave through $CC38, which writes the item table back when it changed (save_item_table $03C2); a purchase that sells out the last item in stock leaves through message 1 ($CBD3, $CBBA) without writing it, and shop_who_enters then clears item_table_changed ($CA53).

Counts what the shop can sell now: items 1-93 (records from $3110, eight bytes apart, item_record for item 1 first) whose stock, record byte 2, is not 0 and whose class is in the shop's list (item_class_in_list $03D1, list at $9D). Returns A = the count, and $D1 = the last item counted, the line list_line_label marks with '_' instead of '>'. Item 94, the table's last record ($33F8), is never looked at.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $CC78: the item count_stock is looking at, set to 1 at $CC5F and stepped at $CC7C up to 94, where the count stops; the LDA copies it to $D1 when the item is in stock and of a class the shop sells.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $CC93, zeroed at $CC67 and incremented at $CC75 for each item on offer: count_stock's result, returned in A.

Per-item routine of the buy list: list_show_page calls it through $47/$48 with A = an item number, 1-93. Declines (carry set, $CCA2) an item whose stock, record byte 2, is 0 or whose class the shop does not sell. Otherwise list_line_label, then in normal video buy_price right-aligned in five columns ($02ED), a space and the item's name in the singular ($38 = 1, print_item_name $03CB); carry clear.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $CCC0, written at $CC96: the item buy_list_line is printing, whose name ends the line.

What the shop pays for the item whose record is at ($16): $1C-$1E = its price (load_price: record bytes 0-1) less price >> $73, the shift from byte 4 of the shop's map record: 1 pays half the price, 2 three quarters, 0 all of it. The shifted part rounds down, so the payment rounds up. Goes on at $CCD4, the arithmetic it shares with buy_price.

What the shop charges for the item whose record is at ($16): $1C-$1E = its price (load_price: record bytes 0-1) less price >> $74, the shift from byte 3 of the shop's map record; every shop record found has 0 there, so items cost their full price. Falls into $CCD4, shared with sell_price: X = 0 leaves the price; otherwise $1C-$1E is shifted right X times and subtracted from the price read again from ($16).
Prints message A of the shop's text block with direct output (output_direct $02FF), each character drawn at once; then as shop_print_wrapped from $CD03.
Prints message A of the shop's text block word-wrapped (output_wrapped $0302): at $CD03 it points $43/$44 at the block, $CD3D, and jumps to print_message ($0311).

Puts the text cursor at column 14, row 2: the first line inside the text window, where the P)ool line and 'That costs too much!' are printed above the list, and 'Your inventory is full.' after a purchase that fills the last free slot ($CC30).
Loads the price of the item whose record is at ($16) into the 24-bit number $1C-$1E: record byte 0 (low) and byte 1 (high), top byte 0.

Prints 'P)ool Money = $' (message 4, direct; its {03} clears the rest of the line) and the trading member's cash (cash_load $0392, print_long $02F0) at column 14, row 2, above the sell or buy list. Its $30 = 8 changes nothing: print_long sets $30 to 8 itself ($1CA9).

The party position (1-7) of the member who is trading: 1 by default ($CA60), else the member picked at 'Who wants to enter?' ($CA75). Read for the roster highlight ($CAA1) and by the 'P' key, which pools every other member's cash on this one ($CB5A, $CC40).

1 after a sale ($CB3B) or a purchase ($CC1D), cleared each time round the shop's loop ($CA53): when set, leaving the sell or the buy list writes the item table at $3100 back to its file (JMP $03C2 at $CB56 and $CC3D), so the stock the shop keeps in byte 2 of each record lasts. A purchase that sells out the last item in stock is the exception: the buy list is then left through message 1 ($CBD3, $CBBA) without the test, the table is not written, and the next time round the loop clears the flag.

0 on entry ($CA25), 1 after any sale ($CB3E) or purchase ($CC20): when set, leaving the shop from 'Who wants to enter?' saves the game ($CA85-$CA8A, $02D8). Left-arrow at 'B)uy or S)ell?' in a party of one jumps past that test ($CA98 to $CA8D), so that way out never saves.

The shop's packed text block (the engine's format; shop_print_wrapped points $43/$44 here). These 60 bytes are its alphabet: entries $00-$23 are ' ', t, o, n, y, e, a, newline, the end code ($00, code $08), u, r, h, s, l, i, w, m, c, $, {06}, '.', ')', v, p, g, f, d, b, '?', ''', '!', {04}, {03}, k, '=', {0B}; codes $00-$1D give entries $00-$1D, the escape code $1F followed by 0-5 gives entries $1E-$23, and code $1E is the capital shift; $24-$3B are unused $7F.
The shop text's group table, three words, each an offset from $CD79 to a group of four messages: +$06 = $CD7F (messages 0-3), +$3E = $CDB7 (4-7), +$8A = $CE03 (8-11).

Shop messages 0-3, one bit stream: 0 empty (never printed); 1 '{04}We are temporarily out of stock.
{06}' (nothing to buy, $CBD3); 2 'Who wants to enter?
' ($CA69); 3 '
{0B} can't buy anything.
{06}' (the member is not conscious, $CA7D). {04} clears the window, {06} waits at '(RETURN)', {0B} is the member's name. Message 3 ends with byte $CDB5; the next byte, $CDB6 ($01), lies before group 1 and is not read.

Shop messages 4-7: 4 'P)ool Money = ${03}' (show_pool_line); 5 '
You don't have anything they want!
{06}' (nothing to sell, $CAD6); 6 '
Do you want to B)uy or S)ell?
' ($CAA7); 7 '{04}
    $$$      ITEM', the list header ($CACE, $CBBB).

Shop messages 8 and 9, the last the shop prints: 8 'Your inventory is full.\n{06}' ($CBB5, $CC33); 9 'That costs too much!{03}' ($CC4D). Message 9's end code is in $CE23; the group's messages 10 and 11 would decode from the bytes after it ('mo', '  t'), and nothing asks for them.

The last byte module 1's own packed data decodes to ($05): the module is $CA00-$CE24, 1,061 bytes, the same on sides 1, 2 and 4. It follows message 9's end code ($CE23) and nothing reads it: the shop prints messages 1-9 only, and no instruction or pointer in the module reaches past $CE23.

$CE25-$CE78: not module 1. The unpacker decodes a 4-page read window ($CE), not the stream's length, and on side 1 (this snapshot) module 3's stream begins 947 bytes into module 1's, so $CE25-$CE60 are module 3's packed bytes decoded with module 1's table, and $CE61-$CE78, 24 zeros, come from the zero bytes after module 3's stream (T25/L8 bytes $7D-$98), where the window ends. Nothing reads them.
